name: CA-28
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+14 partisan lean favors Democrats heavily
Chu holds a massive cash advantage ($3.7M vs $205K)
Long-serving incumbent with no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price Chu's re-election near 97%
model.rationale: The district's strong Democratic lean, Chu's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing her re-election at roughly 97% all point the same direction, leaving Verlato with too little money or outside help to close a twenty-plus-point gap.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Verlato or a sharp national shift against Democrats could narrow the margin, though an upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 28th District leans strongly Democratic, and incumbent Judy Chu has held the seat since 2009. She advanced to the general election against Republican April Verlato, a challenger with limited resources. Chu has raised about $930,000 and holds $3.7 million in cash, while Verlato has raised roughly $250,000 with $205,000 on hand. Outside spending has been negligible, with only token support for the incumbent and none against her.

No public polls cover the contest and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals. Prediction markets price Chu's re-election at roughly 97 percent. The combination of a D+14 partisan lean, a well-funded incumbent, and a lightly funded challenger makes Verlato's path to an upset very narrow, and the seat is rated Safe Democratic.
